commit.message: fix(memory): reject embedded Hermes entry delimiter (MAGI-001)

specification.objective: MAGI-001: reject the complete Hermes memory entry delimiter in all Magi-controlled new content before invoking public MemoryStore operations or accepting compacted AI proposals; diagnose preexisting values without editing them. Preserve Magi 1.7.8 and Hermes contracts.

requirements.statement: Validate any Magi-controlled add/replace content for the exact Hermes entry delimiter before native mutation, in memory and user.
Reject AI compaction proposals embedding the delimiter, retry generation when possible and block apply prior to calling apply_batch.
Reject any invalid pending add/replace proposal when Magi controls its approval; allow rejection of invalid proposals and do not modify legacy entries automatically.
Preserve normal Unicode, isolated section signs, multiline entries, pins, budgets, fingerprints, public native APIs and version 1.7.8; document diagnostic and limitations.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Tests demonstrate both targets reject content containing the complete delimiter before store add/replace and allow ordinary Unicode/newlines/isolated section signs.
Compaction previews containing embedded delimiter retry or fail safely; crafted apply requests containing delimiter never call batch.
Pending approvals cannot persist add/replace content containing delimiter and rejects remain possible.
Existing tests and POLIS gates pass; changelog and compatibility notes describe Magi-only protection without upstream guarantees.

invariants.statement: Do not write MEMORY.md or USER.md directly, only public existing Hermes APIs.
No change to Hermes or plugin version; preserve valid memory actions and existing UX.

forbidden_states.statement: Magi persists an embedded complete entry delimiter in new memory content.
Magi claims that this prevents all Hermes writers from persisting invalid serialization.

inputs.statement: TASKS.md MAGI-001; compatibility note describing existing delimiter round-trip failure.

outputs.statement: Magi-specific shared validation, API and compaction protections with targeted regressions.

failure_semantics.statement: Reject invalid content before native mutation and return explicit safe error; if AI output invalid, retry or return no-change/error.
